components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; height: 52px; padding: 14px 32px; background: #000000; color: #f5f3f1; font: 500 14px/1.5 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; border: 0; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0 4px 6px -1px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0 2px 4px -2px; transition: box-shadow 0.25s ease, transform 0.25s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: rgba(0,0,0,0.06) 0 12px 28px -8px, rgba(0,0,0,0.03) 0 4px 12px -4px; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #000000; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Button
components.description: Secondary action: sans at 75% opacity with a hairline underline.

narrative.overview:
The site is a monochrome algorithm sheet: black ink on warm paper in light mode, off-white signal on terminal black in dark mode. Structure comes from hairline rules and uppercase Geist type, metadata from Geist Mono's machine voice, and proof of craft from kinetic typography — letters that assemble, clip-path wipes that develop like printed panels, and a marquee that ticks like a status line. There is no color story beyond one red pixel; the drama is weight, tracking, and the hairline grid.

The system is dual-theme by design: every token flips between a paper world (#F5F3F1 ground, #000000 ink) and a terminal world (#0F0F10 ground, #F5F5F5 ink) via data-theme on the root element. The accent is not a hue — it is the ink itself, inverted per theme.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome: ink, paper, hairlines; red confined to text selection and one favicon pixel.
Two voices: Geist for reading prose, Geist Mono (uppercase, wide tracking) for every label, status, period, and coordinate.
Sharp geometry: 0px corners everywhere except 8px icon controls.
Hairline structure: 1px borders divide rows, sections, and panels; never fills.
Kinetic reveals: staggered letter assembly, clip-path wipes, marquee band — all reduced-motion safe.

rules.name: The One Red Pixel Rule
rules.body: Red (#dc2626 light / #ff7575 dark) appears only in ::selection and the favicon's single pixel — under 1% of any screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Ink Inversion Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is not a new palette: every token inverts (ink becomes paper, paper becomes ink); hue, saturation, and structure stay identical.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Every non-prose string is Geist Mono, uppercase, tracked 0.08em or wider. If a reader can parse it as data, it is mono.

rules.name: The Comment Prefix Rule
rules.body: Machine-voice status lines are prefixed // — the sheet's signature comment motif.

rules.name: The Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows are ambient micro-lifts reserved for interactive controls at rest and on hover. Static content is always flat.

dos: Do keep red to ::selection and the favicon pixel — one red element per build, never more.
Do set every label, status, period, and coordinate in Geist Mono uppercase with 0.08em+ tracking.
Do divide rows, sections, and panels with 1px hairline borders — structure by line, not fill.
Do observe reveals through unclipped wrappers (ClipReveal pattern) so IntersectionObserver sees partial visibility.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: mount-state animations skip, CSS animations collapse to 0.01ms, smooth scroll turns off.
donts: Don't add gradients, glows, colored accents, or any hue beyond the one red pixel.
Don't round corners beyond the 8px icon-control exception.
Don't place micro-labels above headings as eyebrows — headings carry themselves; metadata lives in the mono voice below or beside.
Don't use hard offset shadows — this world's shadows are soft ambient lifts on controls only.
Don't split the type system: Geist reads, Geist Mono labels; nothing else ships.
